'''The Brothers''', or simply '''Brothers''', was a group of [[Slaver/Legends|slaver]] zealots and one of the five ruling organizations on [[Mek-Sha]] after [[Huttbreaker's Rebellion]]. They sold many [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]] to the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] by [[3627 BBY]].

==Organization==
{{Quote|Labor is purpose. Labor is clarity. Labor is freedom. Idleness is the enemy. It beckons, whispers cloying promises of happiness and comfort. Reject it! Idleness leads not to happiness, but to confusion.|Brothers' [[Datapad/Legends|datapad]]|<ref name="The Value of Labor">{{TORcite|exp=ons|type=general|The Value of Labor|Mek-Sha}}</ref>}}
The Brothers were a ruthless and enigmatic [[Slaver/Legends|slaver]] organization operating in [[Mek-Sha]] in [[3627 BBY]],<ref name="Codex" /> based in the [[Brothers Oversight Center]].<ref name="Brothers Center" /> They were zealots who worshipped labor and considered it freedom as opposed to idleness, which they deemed their enemy. The Brothers deemed [[Refugee/Legends|war refugees]] as agents of idleness and hence captured and sold them off as [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]], turning them into forces of labor.<ref name="The Value of Labor" /> The slavers opposed the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], which forbid slavery, and worked with the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]], becoming their best clients. Through the slave trade, the group became extremely wealthy.<ref name="Codex" />

The group was severely weakened when [[Arn Peralun]], a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], having developed a deep hate for slavery on [[Dakot Seven]], gave into his anger and slew many of the Brothers without his [[Tau Idair|master's]] consent. [[Lana Beniko]] believed that this sudden development would severely harm the Sith Empire's war efforts amid the [[third Galactic War]].<ref name="Brothers">{{TORcite|exp=ons|type=general|Brothers Keeper|Mek-Sha}}</ref>
